name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,788

entries.clue: Steal animal's morsel (7)

blocks.note: to snip is slang for to nick or pinch, i.e. steal
a pet is a domestic animal; the 's joins it on

annotation.surface: A thief makes off with some creature's dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive 's reads as ownership of the morsel, but it only glues PET onto SNIP.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name a small piece or scrap of something, usually snipped off a larger whole.

entries.clue: Mo Salah's top clips noted abroad (5,6)

indicatorNotes.top: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.abroad: letters sent abroad are scattered far and wide, out of their order

blocks.note: first letter of Salah
CLIPS NOTED rearranged

annotation.surface: Highlights of the Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah, watched in foreign countries.
annotation.walkthrough: Mo reads as Mohamed Salah's nickname, but it is the short word for a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British 'mo' is short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'; both mean an instant of time.

entries.clue: At home, one assumes Mum exercises well (2,5)

indicatorNotes.assumes: to assume is to put on, like a garment, so SH goes on top of A

blocks.note: in = at home
mum = silent, as in 'keep mum'; SH asks for silence
a = one
PE = physical education, school exercises

annotation.surface: A child notes that their mother, who works out, is fit and at home.
annotation.walkthrough: Mum looks like a mother; here it means silent, the sense in 'mum's the word'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone fit and healthy is in good physical condition, i.e. well.

entries.clue: Prunes and other fruit delivered (5)

indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered, so the word is spoken rather than written

blocks.note: pears are fruit other than prunes

annotation.surface: Prunes and more fruit arrive by delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: Prunes looks like a fruit, which makes 'other fruit' natural, but it is the verb: to cut back.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a gardener who prunes trims or cuts back growth, just as a cook trims peel.

entries.clue: Extremely anxious fool's suspect ethics (10)

indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands, so rearrange

blocks.note: a twit is a fool; the 's joins it on
ETHICS rearranged

annotation.surface: A fool with dodgy morals becomes deeply nervous.
annotation.walkthrough: Suspect reads as describing the fool's morals; it is telling you to rearrange ETHICS.
annotation.definitionFit: Twitchy is informal for nervous and jumpy; the superlative form matches 'extremely'.

entries.clue: Perhaps Norma had some food - a common function (7)

indicatorNotes.Perhaps: perhaps signals that Norma is one example of a wider class
indicatorNotes.common: held in common: the A is shared by both words and written once

blocks.note: Norma is Bellini's OPERA; its final A is the shared one
the A both words have in common
ATE = had some food, its A already supplied

annotation.surface: A woman called Norma took a bite, as everyone does.
annotation.walkthrough: OPERA and ATE overlap on one A, and 'a common' tells you to write it once.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a machine that works or runs is functioning.

entries.clue: Not yet settled or not quite married? (4)

blocks.note: a bill still outstanding, not paid off
read as O plus WED: a nought before 'married', so nothing like wed

annotation.surface: A couple whose relationship is unresolved: are they married or not?
annotation.walkthrough: Settled suggests settling down with a partner, but it means paid. The question mark flags the whimsical O-WED reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding remains unpaid; the second half is a playful split into a zero and a wedding.

entries.clue: Once abstinent drifter admitted becoming party animal? (9)

indicatorNotes.admitted: TT admits, or lets in, the drifter, so ROVER goes inside

blocks.note: ex = former, once
TT = teetotal, abstaining from drink
a rover wanders about

annotation.surface: A reformed drinker, once a wanderer, lets loose and becomes the life of the party.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks party animal as a loose, playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an outgoing, sociable person is the sort who loves a party.

entries.clue: Fits current trousers (7)

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
cords = corduroy trousers

annotation.surface: A shopper finds that today's fashionable trousers fit.
annotation.walkthrough: Fits and current both pose as clothing words; current is electricity.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to agree or be consistent with, as a story matches the facts.

entries.clue: Flip cover that's slippery (3)

annotation.definitionNote: slippery is an adjective; with 'that's' it describes the thing, a noun

indicatorNotes.Flip: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word runs back up

blocks.note: lee = shelter, cover from the wind

annotation.surface: A lid that flips over turns out to be slick.
annotation.walkthrough: Flip cover suggests a phone case; cover is shelter, as in the lee of a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the fish's smooth, mucus-coated skin makes it proverbially hard to grasp.

entries.clue: Nobody's free to swap spectacles for monocle 'by right' (5)

indicatorNotes.swap: to swap is to exchange: two lenses (OO) traded for one lens (O)
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so R is placed next to the rest

blocks.clueFragment: free to swap spectacles for monocle
blocks.note: LOOSE (free) with OO, two lenses, replaced by O, one lens
R = right

annotation.surface: A nobody may trade their glasses for an eyeglass, as is their right.
annotation.walkthrough: OO looks like a pair of spectacles and O like a monocle, so the swap turns LOOSE into LOSE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an unsuccessful, insignificant person is dismissed as a nobody.

entries.clue: Papers misrepresented a client's twin (9)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, out of their proper order

blocks.note: ID = identity papers
A CLIENT rearranged

annotation.surface: Newspapers got a client's twin sibling wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Papers are identity documents, not newspapers; twin is an adjective here.
annotation.definitionFit: As adjectives both mean exactly matching, as twin beds or matching pairs are.

entries.clue: Negotiate gender reassignment legislation? (8)

blocks.note: trans = transgender
an act is a piece of legislation

annotation.surface: Politicians haggle over a law on changing gender.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is being split playfully into a law about gender.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to conduct business or carry through a deal.

entries.clue: Foul made by Rodri in action against Hearts (6)

indicatorNotes.in action: something in action is moving about, so Rodri's letters shift
indicatorNotes.against: against can mean up next to, so H is placed beside the result

blocks.note: H = hearts, the card suit
RODRI rearranged

annotation.surface: A match report: the midfielder Rodri commits a foul against the Scottish club Hearts.
annotation.walkthrough: Foul is the football offence in the surface but the adjective nasty in the answer. Hearts is an Edinburgh football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as adjectives: nasty, very unpleasant or disgusting.

entries.clue: Conflict in shared bedroom occupied by bewildered setters (6,5)

indicatorNotes.occupied by: a room occupied by people has them inside it, so the dorm holds the letters
indicatorNotes.bewildered: the setters are confused, their letters jumbled

blocks.note: a dorm (dormitory) is a shared bedroom
SETTERS rearranged

annotation.surface: Confused crossword setters squabble in the dormitory they share.
annotation.walkthrough: Operation Desert Storm was the 1991 Gulf War campaign.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1991 Gulf War operation against Iraq was a military conflict.

entries.clue: Teenage gamine periodically sought for modelling contract (10)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods: take every other letter
indicatorNotes.modelling: modelling clay is shaping it, so the letters are shaped into a new form

blocks.note: taken as it stands
G_M_N_ from gamine

annotation.surface: A young, boyishly slim girl is scouted for a modelling deal.
annotation.walkthrough: Modelling belongs to the fashion picture, but it is the instruction to reshape the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A performer's booking or job is an agreed arrangement, a contract for work.

entries.clue: Face-lift: what does it achieve? (9)

blocks.note: one face of a building, as an architect draws it
raising, a lift
surface padding: a question whose joking answer is the entry itself

annotation.surface: A question about what cosmetic surgery actually accomplishes.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen welds two definitions into one cosmetic procedure, and the question adds a third reading: a face-lift achieves elevation.
annotation.definitionFit: An architect's drawing of one side of a building, and also the act of raising something higher.

entries.clue: Sex during tap dancing used contorting abilities (9)

indicatorNotes.during: during means in the course of, so IT falls within the two rearranged words
indicatorNotes.dancing: letters that dance move about, so TAP takes a new order
indicatorNotes.contorting: to contort is to twist out of shape, so USED is twisted

blocks.note: TAP rearranged
it = sex, as in 'doing it'
USED rearranged

annotation.surface: A cheeky picture of tap dancers showing off how flexible they are.
annotation.walkthrough: Tap dancing reads as the dance style, but dancing is an instruction applied to TAP.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: natural talents or skills, a knack for doing something.

entries.clue: Drops off suits when leaving Poland (5)

indicatorNotes.when leaving: leaving means departing, so the letters for Poland depart the word

blocks.note: suits = pleases, as in 'that suits me'
PL is the international code for Poland; removed

annotation.surface: Someone nods off whenever it's convenient to depart from Poland.
annotation.walkthrough: Suits reads as clothing or court cases; it is the verb, pleases.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: lessens or slackens, as rain or demand gradually declines.

entries.clue: Corporation's e-ticketing limits start (5)

indicatorNotes.limits: to limit is to bound, so the phrase holds the answer within its bounds

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Corporation's into the start of e-ticketing

annotation.surface: A company's electronic ticketing puts caps on something.
annotation.walkthrough: Limits reads as restrictions on e-ticketing; it means contains.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the beginning of something, especially an illness or winter.

entries.clue: Queen interrupting settles protests (7)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in, so QU breaks into the middle of SEALS

blocks.note: seals = settles, as in 'seal the deal'
Qu. is an abbreviation for queen

annotation.surface: The monarch steps in to calm down demonstrations.
annotation.walkthrough: Protests looks like a noun for demonstrations; it is the verb, complains.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: complains loudly, objects shrilly to something unfair.

entries.clue: Darker Cornish paintings maybe more popular if very quietly forgotten (9)

indicatorNotes.maybe: maybe signals that paintings are one example of a wider class
indicatorNotes.forgotten: what is forgotten is left out, so PP drops from the word

blocks.note: Cornwall is in the South West (SW) of England
paintings are art

blocks.clueFragment: more popular if very quietly forgotten
blocks.note: HIPPIER (more popular, trendier) without PP, the musical mark for very quietly

annotation.surface: Cornish paintings might sell better if they were a bit darker and less muted.
annotation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion or skin; the comparative form matches 'darker'.

entries.clue: Frozen wildernesses found over in Room 101 (3,4)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over in a down entry, the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: room = space
CI = 101 in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Icy wastes turn up inside Orwell's torture chamber, Room 101.
annotation.walkthrough: Room 101 is the torture room in Orwell's 1984, but the clue splits it into ROOM and 101.
annotation.definitionFit: Polar sheets of permanent ice cover huge uninhabited regions, frozen wastes.

entries.clue: Suspects party underlings blame the SNP's leaders (6)

indicatorNotes.leaders: leaders go at the front, so take the leading letter of each word

blocks.note: a do is a party
first letters of underlings, blame, the, SNP's

annotation.surface: Party juniors point the finger at the Scottish National Party's leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: Leaders looks like party bosses, but it picks the first letter of each word. The SNP is the Scottish National Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: mistrusts, is inclined to disbelieve something.

entries.clue: Takes off underpants in interviews? (8)

blocks.note: briefs are underpants, and the prefix de- means remove
questions someone after a mission

annotation.surface: Someone removes their underwear during questioning.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a pun: read the answer as DE-BRIEFS, and the question mark admits it.
annotation.definitionFit: Questioning an agent or soldier after a completed mission; the joke half reads it as removing briefs.

entries.clue: Wild storm engulfs the centre of Newbury (5)

indicatorNotes.engulfs: to engulf is to swallow up, so RAID closes around the letter
indicatorNotes.centre: the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: to storm a place is to raid it
middle letter of NEWBURY

annotation.surface: A fierce storm sweeps over the middle of the Berkshire town of Newbury.
annotation.walkthrough: Wild and storm pose as weather; storm is the verb, to attack.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: frenzied and uncontrolled, like a dog with rabies.

entries.clue: Expressions of excitement issue over the Tannoy (4)

indicatorNotes.over the Tannoy: a Tannoy is a public address system, so the word is spoken

blocks.note: to ooze is to issue, seep out

annotation.surface: An announcement over a loudspeaker sets off gasps of delight.
annotation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a noun, a problem; it is the verb, to flow out.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the delighted gasps a crowd lets out at fireworks.

entries.clue: Showy elderly relative does initially impressive cartwheels (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
indicatorNotes.cartwheels: the letters turn head over heels

blocks.note: gran = grandmother
DOES plus I, the first letter of impressive, rearranged

annotation.surface: A flamboyant grandmother pulls off some remarkable cartwheels.
annotation.walkthrough: The gran doing cartwheels is the joke; cartwheels is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pretentiously grand, designed to impress, ostentatious.

entries.clue: Fishy item in bagging area (3)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the answer sits within the phrase

blocks.note: the last letter of bagging and the first two of area

annotation.surface: The self-checkout machine complains of an unexpected item in the bagging area.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the self-checkout warning 'unexpected item in bagging area'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a long-snouted freshwater fish, so a fishy item.

entries.clue: Vote against party (5)

blocks.note: voting against means casting a negative ballot, read as a three-word phrase
a celebration, not a political party

annotation.surface: Voting against a political party.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A NO for the first half. Party reads as political, but a beano is British slang for a knees-up.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for a noisy celebration or knees-up; split into three words it is what a dissenting voter does.

entries.clue: Checks Nadal's OK to be introduced to supporters (7)

indicatorNotes.to be introduced to: introduced to means put into, so SI goes inside RESTS

blocks.note: rests = supports, as for a snooker cue
si is Spanish for yes; Rafael Nadal is Spanish

annotation.surface: Rafael Nadal is happy to be introduced to his fans.
annotation.walkthrough: Nadal is the Spanish tennis player, so his OK is the Spanish si.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: holds back or withstands, as a dam stems a flood.

entries.clue: Healthy reward a few gathered after clean-up (4,3)

indicatorNotes.gathered: what you gather is what you hear, as in 'I gather'
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so this part comes second

blocks.note: a tidy is a clean-up
some = a few

annotation.surface: A handful of volunteers collect a generous payment after a litter pick.
annotation.walkthrough: Gathered looks like collecting people; it means heard, as in 'I gather'.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a large amount of money, so a generous payment or prize.
